source_text: Long-term medical complications from khatna, the form of female genital cutting practiced primarily in India's Dawoodi Bohra community and classified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as Type 1 (partial or total removal of the clitoral prepuce), include scarring, keloid formation, and chronic infections due to tissue damage and impaired healing. [7]
